# CUNEF Server User Guide {.home-title .unnumbered .unlisted}

[Basic usage, Conda environments, jobs, GPUs, and reproducible workflows]{.home-subtitle}

::: {.byline}
By [Roi Naveiro](https://roinaveiro.github.io/){.author}, Assistant Professor, CUNEF Universidad\
For CUNEF faculty and research staff · Revised 27 November 2026 · [PDF version](assets/cunef-slurm-user-guide.pdf)
:::
:::

This guide explains how to use `naranjito`, the shared compute server of CUNEF Universidad. It intentionally starts with the minimum commands needed to run one job, then adds resource selection, environments, arrays, GPUs, and troubleshooting.

::: {.specs}
Host
: `naranjito.cunef.edu`, reachable from the CUNEF network or through the VPN

Processors
: Two Intel Xeon 6740E, 192 cores (184 available to jobs)

Memory
: 256 GB (about 212 GB available to jobs)

GPUs
: Four NVIDIA L40S, 48 GB each

Scheduler
: Slurm, with the partitions `general`, `interactive`, and `preemptible`

System
: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
:::

All of it is shared by everyone through the Slurm scheduler. You log in, prepare your code and environment, and then ask Slurm to run the work through `sbatch` or `srun`. Everywhere in this guide, replace `<username>` with your own CUNEF server user name.

## About {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This guide is written and maintained by [Roi Naveiro](https://roinaveiro.github.io/), Assistant Professor at CUNEF Universidad. It follows the practical structure of established university HPC documentation while adapting every example to `naranjito`. Corrections and suggestions are welcome through the [issue tracker](https://github.com/cunef-hpc/cunef-hpc.github.io/issues).
